title: Auth Control Plane endpoint authentication profile (v1 wire format)
description:
The machine-readable authentication profile one route exports (TRD section 10). It states what the route ACCEPTS: credential classes, token requirements, assurance, action, resolvers, cache and impersonation behaviour, entitlement input, and how a denial is disclosed. It is the language-neutral contract the auth-service's route registry, the CI profile gate and every resource service read.

RULED REFERENCE, NOT REUSE OR REDEFINE (lead ruling on CHAOS-4931, 2026-10-17, from chris's 'Duplicating data makes ZERO sense'). Where this profile and another contract mean the SAME thing by a field, the field is a `$ref` into the file that owns it, never a copy: `classification` into the Wave-0 inventory schema (endpoint-profile.schema.json); credential class, issuer, audience, assurance and action syntax into principal.v1. So the credential-class vocabulary is defined once (principal.v1's enum, which a guard test already holds equal to credential-classes.json in both directions), and an unknown class fails here for the same reason it fails there. Fields whose MEANING differs from the inventory (the inventory records what exists today as free text with gaps; this profile states what the new service accepts as closed tokens) are defined here and are not references: resource_resolver, tenant_requirement, cache_class, impersonation, denial_disclosure, token.algorithm.

EVERY VOCABULARY IS CLOSED. An unknown credential class, action syntax, resolver, tenant requirement, cache class, impersonation mode or disclosure mode is a validation error, not an extension point (G-26: unknown denies). This is the control for CHAOS-3271, where a middleware parsed a valid opaque ACR credential as a user JWT: the class is declared per route and `class_disambiguator` makes a multi-class route say HOW the class is chosen, so a validator can never be found by trying each in turn (TRD section 2 principle 1).

WHAT THE SCHEMA CANNOT SAY, stated so nobody assumes it does: (1) it cannot prove the declared action is in the registered action vocabulary (ACP-ADR-05: that is derived from the inventory and source review); the profile gate checks membership. (2) it cannot prove `class_disambiguator.name` is unique per class or that every accepted class has a marker. (3) it cannot prove `route` is mounted. Those are gate checks over the registry, not wire-shape checks.

No integer field exists on purpose: the integer-guard hazard in README.md (a float with a zero fraction validates as an integer) does not apply to a document with no integers, and cache lifetime is a closed class rather than a number of seconds.

schema_version.description: Identifies this document's contract. A relying party MUST reject an unrecognised value rather than parse optimistically (G-26). TRD section 21: additive within v1; breaking semantics need v2.

method.description: HTTP verb, upper case, closed. TRD section 15 lists exactly these.

route.description: Route pattern as registered, e.g. /v1/memberships/{id} or /v1/authorize:batch. ASCII path characters only, so a profile cannot carry a query string, a host or whitespace. Written as an explicit class and never \d/\w/\s (Unicode in Python re, ASCII in Go RE2 and ECMA-262).

classification.description: protected or public, referenced from the Wave-0 inventory schema so the two formats cannot disagree on the closed set.

public_rationale.description: Why this route is public. Required exactly when classification is public: a route with no credential gate needs a stated reason, as in the inventory.

accepted_credential_classes.description: Credential classes this route accepts, each from the closed vocabulary owned by principal.v1 (itself held equal to credential-classes.json plus the documented Wave 1 additions). Empty only for a public route; a protected route needs at least one. An unknown class is a validation error. More than one class requires class_disambiguator.

kind.description: How the class is chosen from the request BEFORE any validator runs: the Authorization scheme, a fixed credential prefix, a dedicated header, the `alg` field of the JWT protected header (compared exactly; query-api picks its Bearer verifier this way, so with the edge verifier unconfigured an HS256 token is refused rather than misrouted), or a signature header. Closed on purpose: there is no 'try each validator' value, because validator fan-out is the CHAOS-3271 defect.

name.description: The scheme, prefix or header name the selector reads. A name, never a credential value.

class_disambiguator.description: REQUIRED when more than one class is accepted. Declares the selector that picks the class. Without it a multi-class route can only be served by fan-out.

token_type.description: Exact expected JOSE `typ`, e.g. at+jwt (TRD section 11).

algorithm.description: Exact expected signing algorithm. EdDSA for platform tokens (TRD section 11); HS256 only for compatibility-enabled legacy profiles (TRD section 16). `none` and every other value are unrepresentable.

token.description: Issuer, audience, type and algorithm a signed token must carry, all four together or none. Issuer and audience are the exact pinned values (G-13); principal.v1 owns their definition. REQUIRED when any accepted class is a signed token whose pins this schema can express, and FORBIDDEN otherwise, so the two directions agree (the pinned classes are user_access_token, workload_token, ops_access_token_hs256, ops_refresh_token, acr_web_assertion, effective_principal_envelope: EdDSA or HS256 JWTs; the rules are the first two allOf branches); a route accepting one of them with no pins would accept any token of that class from any issuer, audience or algorithm. Omit for opaque and signature classes, which have no issuer or algorithm. A signed class whose algorithm or envelope is outside the `algorithm` enum (auth_js_browser_session is an encrypted JWT, acr_workload_identity_exchange and github_app_installation_token carry RS256 JWTs) cannot be described by this profile yet, so `accepted_credential_classes` REFUSES them rather than accepting them without pins; supporting one means widening `algorithm` and moving the class into the pinned list together, a deliberate amendment.

tokens.description: Per-class token pins, keyed by credential class id, for a route that accepts two or more pinned signed classes (the single `token` block holds one algorithm, so classes with different algorithms need one block each). REQUIRED when two or more pinned classes are accepted, FORBIDDEN otherwise, and never beside `token`: exactly one of the two carries the pins. The key set must equal the pinned classes in accepted_credential_classes: one rule per pinned class (the last allOf rules) requires its key when the class is accepted and refuses it when not; a key outside the pinned classes is refused by additionalProperties.

minimum_assurance.description: Lowest authenticator assurance level the route accepts. Absent means no assurance requirement (not applicable), never a default of aal1.

action.description: The registered action this route performs, e.g. members.invite. Same syntax as principal.v1 actions (a bare name such as `admin` is invalid). REQUIRED for a protected route; meaningless on a public one.

resource_resolver.description: How the target resource is resolved. Caller-supplied values are hints, never authority (TRD section 2 principle 3), so the profile names the single trusted source.

tenant_requirement.description: What tenant relationship the principal must hold: an active membership in the resolved organization, a platform role, or none.

current_state_required.description: True when the decision must read current state (membership, grants, impersonation, credentials, keys, billing, roles, destructive operations: TRD principle 6). A boolean, so absence cannot be mistaken for false: the field is required on a protected route.

cache_class.description: TRD section 14 allow-cache class: none, up to 30 seconds decision-bound (low-risk read), or up to 30 seconds resource and revision-bound (repository or evidence read). The 30-second ceiling is a service rule, not a wire value. Tied to current_state_required by the then-branch below.

impersonation.description: Whether a delegated session (actor chain) may call this route. Denied is the safe value; allowed is a deliberate act.

entitlement.description: Entitlement feature key gating the route. Absent means no entitlement input. Authentication, authorization and entitlement are independent gates (TRD principle 2).

denial_disclosure.description: How an authorized-but-denied request is shown: 403 (forbidden) or 404 (not_found, hiding cross-tenant existence, TRD section 18). A missing or invalid credential is always 401 and is not a choice. The error body is error.v1, which carries no resource detail.
